scores.breakdown:
Rubric: GRANDEUR with this kit 26/30, BUILDABILITY 21/25, WORLD COHERENCE 19/20, HERO IMAGES 19/25 (total 85).

GRANDEUR (26/30). This is the engine's sweet spot. One cathedral hall works as a single set: 40 glowBox pillars into FogExp2, beam() shafts, a grid floor, instanced card towers, red emissive pinpoints and rim-lit human() silhouettes. Frames stay 70–85% black with HDR emissives, so the 'darkness is the canvas' rule holds without effort. Three moments are grand by construction: the LIGHTS ON bank ignition (78–81, beams slamming on through fog, one per beat), the worm's-eye 1:166 human under the 300u tower (48), and the rotating red alarm beams in fog (58). Deductions: Act II has 38 s of the same red-tower vocabulary, and 61–76 re-shoots compositions we have already seen. The proofs at 104–105 are a two-bar chart in 3D, which is benchmark-slide syndrome. Six 0.4 s macros of smooth primitives (85, 87, 89, 100, 103 and the 'node blooms' inserts) will read empty without micro-detail.

BUILDABILITY (21/25). Almost everything is a kit primitive.
- Shot 34's camera.up flip at 80° will pop. Approach −89.5° instead.
- Shots 7 and 40 ask for rack focus, but there is no DOF pass.
- Shots 19 and 98 say 'glass', but there is no transmission.
- Shot 98 needs 'thousands of amber threads'. As fatLines that is thousands of draw calls in SwiftShader, so use one LineSegments or instanced thin boxes, or flow().
- Shot 31's 4,096 cursors exceed the instance cap, so render them as particles (square points ARE cursor blocks, which is a happy accident).
- 'Brass' needs an env/strip-light (PMREM of emissive planes) or emissive seams, or metal renders black.
- Recalls 67–74, 106–119 and the bookends need the shared camera modules the writer already flagged.

COHERENCE (19/20). One place, one protagonist light, one colour plot (cold to warm), and angle grammar with meaning. The world never changes metaphor, which is why it will look like a film and not a demo reel.

HEROES (19/25). The 4–6 memorable frames:
1. Human under the red tower (48).
2. The pull-back to one lit box on a dark line (34–35).
3. The bank-by-bank LIGHTS ON down the aisle (78).
4. THE LINE RUNS with the letterbox snapping open (82).
5. The top-down lit factory crane (83).
6. The low-angle foreman obelisk with threads to every station (98).

The foreman is the weakest hero as written ('brass-and-glass', no clear silhouette design), and there is no single Powers-of-Ten scale shot.
fatal_flaws: None fatal. Main risks: Act II visual monotony (red towers re-shot through the 61–76 accelerando plus an 8-shot recall flurry at 67–74), and the foreman obelisk (98) under-designed for the film's #1 hero frame (glass is impossible; thousands of fatLines are too expensive).

scores.breakdown:
Rubric: GRANDEUR 17/30, BUILDABILITY 23/25, WORLD COHERENCE 16/20, HERO IMAGES 15/25 (total 71).

GRANDEUR (17/30). Everything is a cursor rectangle: cursors, gates, walls, the ledger, the monolith and the factory. That makes it the cheapest film to render and the most elegant on paper. On screen, though, it will read as 'emissive rectangles in fog': there is no contrast of forms (no pillars, no beams, no architecture), so scale cues are weak. Act I (8–32 s) is 24 s of ice-blue blinking desks at ASL 1.7 s before the first clay pixel at 24.0. That is exactly the 'very slow' the client rejected. The whip shots that are only 'Blur' (34, 61, 97) are spent shots, not transitions.

BUILDABILITY (23/25). The best of the three. It is all glowBox, particles, fatLines and instanced desks, and the log zoom (19) and wireframe-to-solid build (71) are standard. The only gaps are the 'glass gate' (85, 88–89), for which there is no transmission, and the 20k-particle swarm, which is fine.

COHERENCE (16/20). One motif, rigorously evolved, with match cuts on the rectangle: a smart idea. However, it builds and labels graph, hierarchy and swarm in the cold, letterboxed Act IIC before the drop (72–80), with the camera already righted at 72. That spends the solution imagery before BRAAM #2, so the 92.0 reveal has less to reveal.

HEROES (15/25). The strong frames:
- The giant clay cursor monolith at the head of the line, with banks switching on behind it (86), a true 2001 image.
- The cursor that stops blinking and stays ON (115), the best final image of all three.
- The 16% monument numerals over the lit CODE box (50).
- The swarm slamming the REVIEW wall (54).

Beyond those it is mostly mid-scale blocks.

The Act IIA type is unreadable: '+8 WEEKS / "claude-pilled" · WSJ' is two lines plus a kicker on a 1 s FPV at 2× through a gate (29), and shot 50's card is 8 words.
fatal_flaws: Act I spends 24 s at human-speed cold blues before anything happens. That repeats the 'very slow' failure.
The structure (graph, hierarchy, swarm) is fully shown before the drop, which deflates the Act III reveal.
A rectangle-only world lacks the architectural scale cues that make frames 'grand'.

scores.breakdown:
Rubric: GRANDEUR 24/30 (potential; execution-dependent), BUILDABILITY 12/25, WORLD COHERENCE 13/20, HERO IMAGES 21/25 (total 70).

GRANDEUR (24/30, potential). It has the single best reveal of the three. The ridge is planted three times at 200mm and read as mountains (8, 11, 31). The sea draws back (56–57), 'that's not the horizon.' lands (58), the ridge rises 50× (59), and the wave face ignites radially as structure while the letterbox snaps open on BRAAM #2 (60). That is the bible's 'those aren't mountains' technique done properly. The 16% numerals built from the lamps that stay lit (40) are type-as-image at its best.

BUILDABILITY (12/25). The hero subject is fluid, and this engine has no fluid. Any shot where the wave or sea is the close subject becomes 'particle soup' at the 30k-point cap and 0.75× render: the 30k sine-swell sea (1, 3, 11), the curling wall overhead (4, 33, 98), the barrel FPV (35), the crest as a 'ceiling of light' (20) and the wave breaking over the city with spray (38, 107). Points go sub-pixel at distance and sparse up close. Making it read needs custom displaced geometry and custom shaders per shot. That is the riskiest build of the three, with the highest chance of a 'WebGL demo' look.

COHERENCE (13/20). The metaphors stack up: sea, city of desks, REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY towers, lock gates, slabs rising from the water, and a factory that is also a wave with lattice, tiers and lanes on its face.
- A wave breaking over a city (38, 107) is disaster imagery, and the treatment itself invokes a tsunami. That is a brand risk for an executive launch.
- The same spark plays both Opus 4.5 and Opus 5.5.
- 'OPUS 5.5' is printed at 93.6 s, which dilutes the 120 s title.

HEROES (21/25). The ridge reveal (58–60), the drained sea floor with the lone spark turning toward the horizon (56–57), the 16% dot-matrix numerals (40), the Powers-of-Ten log zoom on '~30,000 agents' (72), and the apex spark beaming to every tier (86).
fatal_flaws: The core imagery (ocean, curling and breaking wave) is fluid sim this engine cannot do. At the 30k-particle cap it will read as noise, not water, and the film's spine depends on it reading.
The climax and peak image is a wave crashing over a city. For a launch film aimed at executives, that is disaster iconography.
Mixed metaphor (sea, city, stations, factory-wave) undermines world coherence.

steal: wave 8/11/31 + 58–60 ('those aren't mountains'): in the machine hall, plant the dark, unlit foreman/ziggurat as a telephoto-compressed 'end wall' behind the code tower in Act I (machine 9, 26, 32), fogged to 80% so it reads as architecture. At the foreman reveal (machine 95–98), light it radially from the centre as wave 60 does. It costs almost nothing to build and gives the reveal a planted payoff.

wave 72 (Powers-of-Ten log zoom): one orb → a lane → the whole hall at 30k points, top-down, power2.inOut on log distance, with '~30,000 AGENTS AT ONCE · ANTHROPIC'. Place it in Act III BEFORE the foreman (around 92–97) so it is never read as an Opus 5.5 result. This gives the machine the scale shot it lacks. Pay for its words by trimming the station labels (drop DESIGN/OPERATE).

wave 40 (dot-matrix numerals from lit instances): build monument type out of the scene's own lights instead of overlay. Use it for machine 26 ('≈5' formed by DARK gaps in the 1,000-orb top-down; invert wave 29's error, where lit numerals on an 80%-lit field are unreadable) and/or as the 16% read on machine 35 (the CODE segment's rails resolve into '16%').

signal 115 (the cursor stops blinking and stays ON, with a localized flare on the final sting): make this machine's last picture after 'BUDGETS IN EARLY 2027.', replacing the black ring-out at machine 125. It is the best closing image in any treatment and nearly free to render.

signal 9 + the rectangle match-cut chain: make the machine cold-open rewind (8) collapse to ONE clay cursor ▮, centred, and match-cut it into machine 9's far station. Also shape-match the drop's cursor ▮ (machine 77) to the first light-bank rectangle at the same screen position (machine 78), and the foreman core (machine 120) to the title light-line slot (machine 122).

signal 101 (one shot, card swap at mid-shot: 'FABLE 5.1-LEVEL WORK.' → '−40% COST VS OPUS 5 · ANTHROPIC'): replaces machine 104+105. It keeps the claim pair together (facts) and kills one bar-chart shot.

signal 95→96 (the same 100 orbs snap into 12 sub-lead clusters, then snap flat into one sheet on the next cut): a literal two-beat version of 'picked their own structure'. Use it if machine 99's split-frame reads muddy at phone size.
signal 71 (wireframe-to-solid station build with a rising scan-line clip, EdgesGeometry + clipping plane): layer it into machine 79–80 so stations visibly 'build' as banks ignite, not just light up.

wave 56–57 (the drained, emptied floor with the protagonist light alone turning toward the horizon): use this composition for the stillness beat at machine 94. Have the hall floor drain of cards with the camera creeping toward the dark centre, instead of a near-black frame with only rim hints.

signal 86 (low-angle symmetric monolith at the head of the line, with banks switching on behind it one per beat): use it as the design reference for machine 98's foreman silhouette. Make it a single clean obsidian monolith with emissive clay seams, strip-light sweep and a light crest, not a vague 'brass-and-glass' obelisk.
cut: machine 19: greeked newsprint 'glass panes'. Unreadable filler, and there is no transmission for glass.
machine 7 and 40: rack focus (there is no DOF pass). Restage 40 with fog depth or a 2D blur on a separate canvasPlane, or cut the 97% progress-bar macro, which reads as stock UI.
machine 59: second slow-motion tower topple. It duplicates 45 a few seconds later.

machine 67–74: trim the 8×0.25 s Act II recall flurry to 4 (like signal 79), or replace it with new escalation. As written, three recall montages (67–74, 106–113, 114–119) make the last 50 s feel like a best-of reel.
machine 104–105: the two-column level/cost bar chart. Merge into one shot with a card swap (signal 101) and a non-chart image.

machine 85, 87, 89, 100, 103: 0.4 s macros of smooth primitives ('node blooms', 'lamp flares'). Either give them real micro-detail (bevels, etched glyphs, scanlines) or cut them and give the time to proof-card read windows.

machine 98 as specified: 'brass-and-glass' (no glass in software GL) and 'thousands of amber threads' as fatLines (too many draw calls). Use one LineSegments, instanced thin boxes or flow() particles.
machine 34: camera.up flip at 80° mid-move. It pops; approach pitch −89.5° instead.
signal 8–24 s: 24 s of ice-blue human-speed desk city before the first clay pixel. It is the 'very slow' failure again.
signal 34, 61, 97: shots whose entire content is 'Blur'. Whips are transitions, not shots.

signal 29 and 27: two-line quote cards plus kicker on 1–2 s FPV and top-down gate shots ('+8 WEEKS / "claude-pilled" · WSJ', '…never felt this much behind…'). Unreadable at that speed and over the word budget.
signal 85, 88–89: glass gates (no transmission in the engine).
signal 49/51 and wave 44: 'THE OTHER 84%?' mapped onto REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY/ON-CALL. Atlassian's remainder includes meetings and other non-delivery time.

wave 1, 3, 4, 20, 33, 35, 38, 98, 107: every shot where a particle ocean or curling or breaking wave is the close subject. It will read as particle soup at the 30k cap, and a wave crashing over a city is disaster imagery.
wave 61: 'IT'S THE NEXT WAVE.' presented as fact (facts.md supports the next wave only as a labelled projection). Also wave 86: 'OPUS 5.5' printed at 93.6 s, before the title.
wave 22: 'blank glowing slabs rise from the water (the world noticing)'. Unreadable abstraction.
wave 29: '≈5 MONTHS' numerals made of lit lamps when 80% of lamps are lit. Illegible; invert it or cut it.
Any standalone 'FABLE 5.1-LEVEL WORK.' card (machine 104, wave 96). It must not be separated from its '40% lower cost vs Opus 5 · Anthropic' qualifier.
fact_problems: machine 99: '100-AGENT TEAMS, SELF-ORGANIZED.' paraphrases the system card's 'picked their own structure'. Use the facts.md wording 'PICKED THEIR OWN STRUCTURE' (signal 95 and wave 87 already do).

machine 104 / wave 96: 'FABLE 5.1-LEVEL WORK.' stands alone on its own card with no source tag. facts.md's claim is a single claim, 'Fable 5.1-level work at 40% lower cost than Opus 5 (Anthropic)'. Splitting it strengthens the capability half, so keep them together with the ANTHROPIC tag.
machine 126: 'MADE BY OPUS 5.5 AGENTS. ONE BRIEF.' facts.md says made WITH Claude Opus 5.5 agents FROM one human brief. 'By' erases the human and strengthens the claim.

machine 25–26: the run-rate (~$9B → $30B+) is company-wide and Anthropic-reported. Rising out of the CODE station's column implies coding revenue, so the ANTHROPIC-REPORTED whisper must stay legible (the writer flagged this).
signal 49/51 and wave 44: 'THE OTHER 84%?' is arithmetic from Atlassian's 16%, and the visuals equate it with delivery stations. The remainder includes meetings and other non-delivery time.
signal 50: the 16% card is 8 words. signal 116: the end credit is 10 words. Both exceed the ≤7-words-per-card rule.

wave 61: 'IT'S THE NEXT WAVE.' states the client's framing as fact. facts.md treats the next wave only as a projection ('If the pattern holds: budgets in early 2027'). Machine deliberately asks 'THE NEXT ONE?' instead.

wave 72: '~30,000 agents at once' is Anthropic-internal (Aug 2026) and predates Opus 5.5. It must never sit adjacent to or inside the Opus 5.5 reveal (fine where wave places it; keep it that way if stolen).
wave 39–40: '16% of lamps stay lit' shows a share of desks or agents, while the claim is about a share of developer TIME. Machine 35's length-proportional sweep is the more accurate visual.
